steps.action:
The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, in which gas molecules in Earth's atmosphere scatter shorter wavelengths of sunlight (blue and violet light) much more strongly than longer wavelengths (red and orange light). Although violet light is scattered even more than blue, our eyes are more sensitive to blue, and some violet light is absorbed in the upper atmosphere, so the sky looks blue rather than violet. This scattered blue light reaches our eyes from all directions across the sky, giving the entire daytime sky its characteristic blue appearance.
